Definition: a bottle (from the gurgling in emptying)
BiblicalUsage: A baqbuq is an earthen bottle, named for the gurgling sound it makes when it is emptied, and Jeremiah is told to take one to the valley of Hinnom and break it before the elders as a sign of how God will break Jerusalem.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the broken bottle is God's plain sermon in clay: a vessel that will not be made whole again is the picture of a city that would not repent.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
